author: EmuCore - Hub
title: xemu hardens NV2A surface handling for empty render regions
summary: An Xbox game can leave the emulated GPU with a surface whose clip region has zero width or height. xemu now skips transfers and CPU access tracking for those surfaces while giving host graphics APIs safe one-pixel placeholders.
heroAlt: Screenshot of the original Xbox dashboard running in the xemu emulator.

blocks.text: A surface can be validly empty

The Xbox NV2A graphics processor exposes color and depth surfaces backed by video memory. A guest can program clipping or dimensions that produce a surface with zero width or height. That state is awkward for a host graphics API, which expects positive image extents and meaningful transfer regions.
Guard each point where pixels move

xemu’s merged change adds zero-dimension checks in both the OpenGL and Vulkan paths. Display lookup, CPU-access callback registration, upload, and download now avoid treating an empty surface as pixel data. The guards cover the points where an invalid extent could otherwise reach a graphics operation.

The Vulkan upload path marks an empty surface initialized before returning. The change also makes callback removal tolerate a null callback, matching the decision not to register one for an empty image. These details keep cleanup and renderer state coherent when the guest creates a surface that has no pixels.

Where an image object still needs an extent, the renderer substitutes one for a zero dimension. That one-pixel allocation is a host-side placeholder; it does not invent guest-visible pixels or turn the empty surface into a drawable region. The PR links the guards to several reports, while noting one report was not reliably reproducible.
